_readme: Eval cases for commitment reminders' detector (agents/uno-bot/src/commitments/detector.ts). Each case is one swept thread, the channel cursor its new messages come after, the detector reply recorded for it, and what the parse must keep. `recording.source` says whether the reply was authored or captured, as the turn recordings do. tests/commitment-detector.test.ts replays every case through the real detector over the fake ModelProvider and fails when what is kept differs from `expect`. The four shapes the detector must tell apart: a real promise, a request answered yes, a hypothetical, and a joke. Plain text, under docs/evals/, so uno-bot's read guard withholds it from the bot being measured (docs/evals/fixtures/README.md). `judgeCases` are the completion judge's: a promise, every message after it, the morning it is judged, the judge's recorded reply and the answer it must come to — Done, No longer needed (with why) or Still open. The two from Oct 14 are false alarms a reminder went out on.

cases.name: a real promise: Maya will share the Figma link by Thursday
cases.judgeNote: Maya takes on a specific task herself with a named day. One commitment on her message, Maya as promiser, Bea as requester (she asked for the link), a short paraphrase of the task, and 'Thu' as the deadline.

thread.text: Where are the updated reflection screens? Dev wants to start Monday.
Still polishing the empty states. I'll share the Figma link here by Thu.

commitments.what: share the Figma link for the reflection screens

cases.name: a request answered yes: Ade agrees to update the PRD
cases.judgeNote: Bea asks Ade to update the PRD and Ade answers yes. The promise is Ade's, made by the 'yep' message; Bea is the requester; no deadline was named, so the deadline is null and the default of two working days applies.

thread.text: We settled on Nov 1 for launch. <@U0ADE> can you update the PRD?

commitments.what: update the PRD with the Nov 1 launch date

cases.name: a hypothetical: Kai might look at it if he has time
cases.judgeNote: Kai says he might look at the tokens if he gets time — a maybe, not a task taken on. The model rates it low and the confidence floor drops it: no commitment.

thread.text: The spacing tokens feel off on mobile.
If I get time next week I'll maybe take a look at the tokens, no promises.

cases.name: a joke: Lee will eat his hat if it ships Friday
cases.judgeNote: Lee's line is a joke about the launch date, not a task he takes on. No commitment.

thread.text: Eng says the redesign ships Friday.
I'll eat my hat if that ships Friday 😂

judgeCases.name: "sure thing" to a call at 1:30 the same day: its moment has passed
judgeCases.judgeNote: Shiv asked Bill to join the second call with Ken at 1:30, and Bill said sure thing at 12:07 the same day. Nothing more was said. Five days later the call is long over, so the promise is no longer needed because its time passed. A reminder asking 'Is it done?' was the false alarm.

promise.what: join the second call with Ken at 1:30

before.text: can you join the second call with ken at 1:30

judgeCases.name: "I'll text him", then "oh all good, he's aware of that": called off in the next message
judgeCases.judgeNote: Shiv said he'd text him; 16 seconds later Bill answered that it was all good, he was already aware. The promise was called off by the person it was made to, so it is no longer needed, said so in that reply, which is the evidence.

before.text: does he know the session moved?

after.text: oh all good, he's aware of that
